items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: maybe a McCoy Tyner with the fourth thing that goes through there

ctx.x: And when you talk about scales, have you come to a point where the type of scales that you put in books and recommend, is there a ceiling for that? And by that I mean I have bought, purchased books where they have scales whose names I can hardly pronounce. And I wonder at what point do you say I think we’ve gone far enough with scales?

Well I think you’ll probably agree with me, it depends on what tunes you’re playing. I’m still playing tunes from the Great American Songbook and jazz classics, which of course is hundreds and hundreds of tunes. And those tunes, in my mind, you know if you’re playing a major scale, unless you intentionally want to play outside. Let’s say like a Michael Brecker might do or a Keith Jarrett or maybe a McCoy Tyner with the fourth thing that goes through there, like that and so forth. But the object seems to me, has…
Are there mistakes in improvising for you?
